plans.name: Spark
plans.audience: Pre-launch or very early-career authors, 0-2 published titles, little to no existing platform (sub-500 email list, sub-1,000 social following), category rank typically outside Amazon top 100,000 or not yet ranking.
plans.positioning: Low-risk entry point — proves whether consistent short-form content can move a specific book before committing budget to a full campaign.
plans.outcome: Establishes a baseline content cadence and click-through data; not expected to independently shift category rank into a visible tier within 90 days.
services: Genre-matched scripts, viral hooks & trending audio
deliverables: No listing, review, or retargeting work included at this tier

plans.name: Enhanced
plans.audience: Authors already running Spark-level content who want one flagship asset (a trailer) to reuse off-platform — in ads, a bio link, a newsletter, or a pitch to reviewers — without yet buying full campaign management. Typically 1-3 books, category rank outside top 50,000.
plans.positioning: Content-plus-asset tier: same cadence as Spark, plus a durable creative asset that compounds across future campaigns rather than disappearing after one post cycle.
plans.outcome: Meaningfully higher reach and CTR than Spark from richer creative alone; still not paired with listing or review work, so conversion lift stays modest.
deliverables: Everything in Spark, plus one cinematic trailer
One long-form video with avatar narration

plans.name: Foundation
plans.audience: Authors with at least one published book and a live Amazon listing that's never been optimized — category rank roughly top 30,000-100,000, no reader list of their own yet, little to no review-driven social proof.
plans.positioning: First tier where the listing itself starts converting the traffic content sends — the entry point to the reader-list ecosystem (ShelfMates/StoryPals).
plans.outcome: Meaningful, sustained rank movement is plausible within a 90-day cycle (loosely, top-100,000 toward top-30,000-50,000 territory for a book with a workable hook), plus the start of an owned reader list.
deliverables: Rewritten listing copy, keywords, and A+ content

plans.name: Starter
plans.audience: Authors with an optimized-or-optimizable listing who are ready to test paid amplification for the first time — usually 1-3 books, category rank top 20,000-60,000, comfortable spending a small, fixed ad budget rather than managing ads themselves.
plans.positioning: Heaviest creative-and-asset tier below full campaign management — 2 trailers, a theme song, and a modest Amazon DSP budget layered on top of Spark-level content.
plans.outcome: Faster impression and CTR growth than Foundation from paid amplification, without the review/preorder/retargeting infrastructure Momentum adds — best read as a bridge tier rather than a launch-campaign tier.
deliverables: Amazon DSP ad spend managed on the author's behalf

plans.name: Momentum
plans.audience: Authors with a specific launch or relaunch coming up and at least one prior book with some sales history — typically fewer than 10 reviews on the target title, category rank top 5,000-20,000, ready for a structured 6-week preorder push.
plans.positioning: First full-funnel tier: content, social proof (ARC reviews), a scheduled preorder campaign, and retargeting run as one coordinated system rather than separate purchases.
plans.outcome: Realistic path to a top-1,000-5,000 category rank around launch week for a book with a workable hook and backlist support; review count roughly doubling via the 10-reader ARC campaign.
services: Segmented retargeting, up to 5x daily for 30 days
deliverables: Full social account management (not just posting)
Segmented retargeting, up to 5x/day for 30 days

plans.name: Growth
plans.audience: Authors with an established backlist (3+ books) scaling an existing readership or mounting an aggressive new launch — typically already inside top 5,000-20,000 in category and pushing toward top 100-1,000, wanting monthly (not quarterly) newsletter placement and a larger review base.
plans.positioning: Top production-and-campaign tier below the fully custom Surge/Orbit engagements — same full-funnel system as Momentum, scaled up in every dimension.
plans.outcome: Realistic path toward top-100-1,000 category rank and bestseller-list visibility for a launch backed by a genuine backlist and reader base; review count growth roughly 2.5x the Momentum tier via the 25-reader ARC campaign.
services: Segmented retargeting, up to 5x daily for 30 days
deliverables: Segmented retargeting, up to 5x/day for 30 days

custom_tiers.note: Custom engagements for multi-book catalogues and bespoke campaign structures.
custom_tiers.pricing_model: custom, dedicated team or custom seat

plan_changes.policy: Upgrading or downgrading is allowed at any time. Current ad spend is taken into account and applied as available credit toward the new plan.

end_of_commitment.policy: On commitment end, everything is handed over via secure transfer if needed — videos created, account info, and related assets. In practice most content is already accessible to the author throughout the engagement, since every content gallery is public to them via their progress-report document/link.

author_involvement.author_provides: A link to the book (or, for a backlist, a link to the author's catalogue), plus optionally any planned discount-deal dates so campaigns can be planned around them.

campaign_management.policy: A dedicated outreach team manages accounts day-to-day, handles ARC/reviewer list outreach, and monitors that campaigns are running smoothly.

genre_support.policy: All genres are supported. Bigger, higher-volume genres tend to see stronger results than smaller genres, simply due to reader pool size.

guarantee.name: Atomic Shelf Commitment
guarantee.summary: Money-back only for demonstrable non-delivery. Everything else is time-based, and we keep working.
covers: agreed deliverables (videos produced, trailers, listing rewrite, ARC recruitment, preorder setup, retargeting activation)
money_back_trigger_conditions: Zero or near-zero impressions after a full cycle despite content being posted as agreed
Zero or near-zero click-throughs despite measurable impressions
Zero measurable results across the full agreed scope — i.e. the work itself was not fulfilled, not merely underperforming
guarantee.money_back_scope: Refund applies only to the specific line items that were not fulfilled at all — not a blanket refund of the full plan price, and not triggered by results that are simply lower than the estimated range.
does_not_guarantee: A specific rank, ranking, or bestseller position
A specific number of sales, preorders, or downloads
guarantee.time_based_remedy: Outside the zero-delivery trigger, results are treated as a function of time and iteration, not a refund event. If a campaign is underperforming its estimated range, Atomic Shelf continues the agreed work, diagnoses what to adjust, and keeps delivering — it does not refund simply because growth is slower than the estimate.
guarantee.remedy: For confirmed non-delivery: refund of the undelivered portion. For underperformance with delivery confirmed: continued work, diagnosis, and adjustment at no extra cost — not a refund.
guarantee.customer_must: Notify Atomic Shelf within 21 days of the end of the applicable campaign cycle (typically the month-3/90-day mark) to claim a refund under the zero-delivery trigger. Claims outside this window are not eligible for the refund remedy, though underperformance concerns are reviewed under the time-based remedy at any time.

review_campaign_disclosure: Planning a free book giveaway? Tell us — preferably in advance. Share your next free-book dates and we'll feature you. You can provide complimentary copies to selected readers, then invite honest, independent reviews. The free copy is never conditional on posting a review, giving a positive rating, or changing an existing review.
results_disclaimer: Expected ranges are 90-day averages based on 200+ books over 24 months, measured against each book's pre-campaign baseline — many starting from little to no prior sales. Individual results vary by genre, backlist, and price point.

proof_metrics.source: Internal campaign performance data from 200+ books over 24 months

case_studies.author: Sarah Mitchell
case_studies.starting_situation: First-time author with no existing platform, category rank outside top 100,000, zero reviews on launch day
case_studies.context: Author had a strong manuscript but no audience. The focus was on discovery and building initial social proof through consistent content and listing optimization.
case_studies.author_quote: I went from having no idea whether anyone would find my book to seeing actual sales and reviews come in. The consistent content made all the difference.

case_studies.author: James Chen
case_studies.starting_situation: Third book in series, existing fanbase but declining sales, category rank top 15,000, wanted to launch stronger
case_studies.context: Author had an established series but needed coordinated launch support. The full Momentum campaign leveraged existing backlist while driving new discovery.
case_studies.author_quote: The preorder campaign changed everything. Having a structured countdown and coordinated content made launch week feel like an event rather than just another release.

case_studies.author: Maria Rodriguez
case_studies.starting_situation: Debut children's author, no existing audience, category rank not established, needed parent/teacher discovery
case_studies.context: Children's books require different discovery channels. The focus was on parent/teacher-facing content and leveraging the trailer for educational contexts.
case_studies.author_quote: The trailer opened doors I didn't expect — libraries and parent groups started sharing it. It gave my book a professional feel that built trust.

pricing_claim_approval.scope: Six-plan pricing structure, commitment discounts, and 90-day performance ranges based on 24 months of internal operating evidence
pricing_claim_approval.evidence_note: All plan metrics are extrapolated from internal performance data across 200+ client books over 24 months. Individual results vary by genre, backlist, and price point.
